description: Registry of MCP servers wired into the hitcon-range-sprint agent framework. Source of truth; see README.md for the wiring policy.

policy.import_mode: reference external snapshot (Security-LabData/external-mcp-tools/<name>) and pin upstream commit, release version, and any submodule commit; do not vendor server source
policy.holder_node: Primary Analysis Gateway (host LabStrix), in a dedicated version-pinned runtime; never the host default interpreter when deps pin an older Python
policy.secrets: environment variables only; never committed; registry records variable names, not values
policy.secret_injection: values live in the gitignored secrets.env at the repo root; a session receives only the names its own entry declares, and only on the host gateway that holds the file
policy.node_placement: one node per server: host gateway (big RAM/disk, repo-local tooling, secrets), flare-vm (Windows artifact parsers, vmrun guest operations), kali (Linux CLI, pcap, document/macro work), container (isolated offensive tooling); never place a server where its data or OS is absent
policy.authorization: command-capable servers (command_exec/write, or an entry that declares no capability at all) are denied until an explicit allowlist entry exists; the decision and its stated reason are audited

authorization.enforcement: security/tools/collab_mcp.py (mcp gate / mcp call); every decision is appended to .collab/runtime/mcp-gate.jsonl

retired.name: semgrep-mcp
retired.reason: Upstream deprecated semgrep-mcp 0.9.0; its tools/list exposed only the deprecation_notice tool. Superseded by the `semgrep mcp` subcommand built into semgrep.

reverified.outcome: Installs on 3.14 (pip 26 accepts the cp39.cp310.cp311 compressed-tag wheel, so the earlier wheel-ceiling claim was wrong) but the pinned semgrep 1.135.0 crashes at runtime on protobuf 4.25.9; after overriding the pin (protobuf 7.36.2, setuptools<81) the server launches and answers initialize with Semgrep/1.12.2, yet tools/list still exposes only the upstream deprecation_notice tombstone and it cannot scan. The same venv's OSS semgrep 1.135.0 also refuses MCP mode (requires Pro Engine). Retirement unchanged; scans come from the semgrep 1.178.0 entry.

previous_source.wheel_tags: semgrep==1.135.0 ships only cp39.cp310.cp311 compressed-tag wheels; pip 26 still installs them on 3.14, the runtime failure is protobuf 4.25.9 upb

servers.name: semgrep
servers.purpose: Current Semgrep MCP server (OSS engine) exposed via the `semgrep mcp` subcommand for code-security scanning.

source.note: server code is bundled in the semgrep package at semgrep/mcp/server.py; no external snapshot or submodule

placement.rationale: needs repo-local file access and the host's cp314-native runtime; the scans are read-only over paths we hand it, so no node hop is worth the copy cost

secrets.note: optional; only needed for platform findings, remote and Pro features

servers.pinned_by: semgrep 1.178.0 ships cp314 wheels, so the host default interpreter runs it natively

servers.name: cve-mcp-server
servers.purpose: CVE/vulnerability intelligence MCP server spanning 20+ sources (NVD, EPSS, CISA KEV, OSV, GitHub Advisory, ...) with a triage_cve orchestrator; aligns with the framework CVE/EPSS/KEV/CVSS research line.

source.snapshot_note: working tree has 2 deleted tracked files (src/cve_mcp/server.py, src/cve_mcp/api/report_generator.py); restored from HEAD into a scratch copy; snapshot itself untouched

placement.rationale: reaches external intelligence APIs and needs the host-held secrets.env; keep it off the VMs so tokens never travel onto the analysis nodes

extra_hard_deps: mcp<2 (snapshot declares mcp[cli]>=1.7.0 which resolves to mcp 2.x and breaks: FastMCP renamed to MCPServer)
